gdp_level.source: Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) quarterly national accounts, OpenSTAT 0012B5BEXQ1 · GDP at current prices, PHP million, not seasonally adjusted, quarterly.
gdp_level.description: The total value of everything the Philippines produces in a year, at current prices, on a rolling four-quarter basis.
gdp_level.real: “Make it real” swaps this to PSA's seasonally adjusted GDP at constant 2018 prices, also quarterly. This strips out the effect of price changes, so it shows genuine output growth rather than growth that's really just inflation.
gdp_level.dollar: “Dollarise” converts each period converted at its own year's PHP/USD rate (World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF, annual average).

gdp_real.source: PSA seasonally adjusted national accounts, OpenSTAT 012B5BEXS1 · GDP at constant 2018 prices, PHP million, seasonally adjusted, quarterly.
gdp_real.description: GDP adjusted for inflation, the same production valued at constant 2018 prices, so changes reflect real output growth rather than price changes.
gdp_real.real: This IS the “Make it real” series, toggling it off shows GDP at current (nominal) prices instead.
gdp_real.dollar: Same historical-rate matching as GDP (current prices): each period converted at its own year's PHP/USD rate.

gdp_growth.source: PSA seasonally adjusted national accounts, OpenSTAT 012B5BEXS1 · change in seasonally adjusted real GDP on the previous quarter, to one decimal place.
gdp_growth.description: How much the economy grew or shrank compared with the previous three months, in real terms, with regular seasonal patterns removed. This is the quarter-on-quarter figure PSA publishes.
gdp_growth.real: This is already a real (inflation-adjusted) growth rate, “Make it real” has no additional effect on it.
gdp_growth.dollar: A growth rate (%) is currency-agnostic, converting the underlying pesos to dollars doesn't change the percentage change. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

gdp_growth_yoy.source: PSA quarterly national accounts, OpenSTAT 0012B5BEXQ1 · real GDP at constant 2018 prices, change on the same quarter a year earlier, not seasonally adjusted.
gdp_growth_yoy.description: How much bigger or smaller the economy is than a year earlier, adjusted for inflation. This is PSA's headline growth figure.
gdp_growth_yoy.dollar: A growth rate (%) is currency-agnostic, converting the underlying pesos to dollars doesn't change the percentage change. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

cpi.source: PSA consumer price index for all income households, 2018=100, OpenSTAT 0012M4ACP23 · all items, change on a year earlier, as published from January 2019; 1995 to 2018 from PSA's 2018-based index (0012M4ACP28).
cpi.description: How much consumer prices are rising compared with a year ago.

cpi_mom.source: PSA consumer price index for all income households, 2018=100, OpenSTAT 0012M4ACP22 · all items, change on the previous month, not seasonally adjusted, to one decimal place.
cpi_mom.description: How much consumer prices moved compared with the month before, from PSA's all-items index.

policy_rate.source: BIS central bank policy rates (WS_CBPOL, M.PH, extended with the daily series D.PH) · Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas' overnight reverse repurchase rate, end of month, from January 2002; the current month shows the latest rate.
policy_rate.description: The policy rate Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas sets to steer borrowing costs. In June 2016 BSP moved to an interest rate corridor and reset the rate from 4.0% to 3.0% as a technical change, not an easing. The BIS series runs back further using earlier money-market rates, which are not shown.

unemployment.source: PSA labour force survey, OpenSTAT 0021B3FKEI2 · unemployment rate, both sexes, not seasonally adjusted, monthly, from January 2021.
unemployment.description: The share of the labour force that wants a job and is actively looking, but can't find one. The survey became monthly in 2021; before that it ran four times a year.

participation.source: PSA labour force survey, OpenSTAT 0021B3FKEI2 · labour force participation rate, both sexes, not seasonally adjusted, monthly, from January 2021.
participation.description: The share of working-age people who are either in work or looking for work. It falls every July and January and recovers the next month, a seasonal pattern in the unadjusted survey.

employment.source: Computed from PSA's labour force survey, OpenSTAT 0021B3FKEI2 · participation rate times PSA's employment rate, both sexes, not seasonally adjusted, monthly, from January 2021.
employment.description: The share of working-age people who are in work. PSA's own "employment rate" is a share of the labour force, so this ratio is computed from PSA's participation and employment rates.

exports.source: IMF international trade in goods (ITG), from PSA · exports of goods, free on board, US$ converted to pesos at the BIS monthly average rate, monthly.
exports.description: The value of goods the Philippines sells to the rest of the world each month, in pesos.
exports.dollar: PSA publishes trade in US dollars; the pesos shown are converted at each month's BIS average rate, and “Dollarise” converts back at that year's World Bank rate.

imports.source: IMF international trade in goods (ITG), from PSA · imports of goods, cost, insurance and freight, US$ converted to pesos at the BIS monthly average rate, monthly.
imports.description: The value of goods the Philippines buys from the rest of the world each month, in pesos.
imports.dollar: PSA publishes trade in US dollars; the pesos shown are converted at each month's BIS average rate, and “Dollarise” converts back at that year's World Bank rate.

trade_balance.source: IMF international trade in goods (ITG), from PSA · exports (free on board) less imports (cost, insurance and freight), US$ converted to pesos at the BIS monthly average rate, monthly.
trade_balance.description: Exports minus imports of goods each month. Below zero means the Philippines buys more from abroad than it sells.
trade_balance.dollar: PSA publishes trade in US dollars; the pesos shown are converted at each month's BIS average rate, and “Dollarise” converts back at that year's World Bank rate.

debt_gdp.source: IMF World Economic Outlook (GGXWDG_NGDP) · general government gross debt, % of GDP, annual · actual years only. The IMF's figures for the years after the one shown are projections, which this site does not publish.
debt_gdp.description: Everything government owes, across all levels of government, compared with the size of the economy.
debt_gdp.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

deficit.source: IMF World Economic Outlook (GGXCNL_NGDP) · general government net lending/borrowing, % of GDP, annual · actual years only. The IMF's figures for the years after the one shown are projections, which this site does not publish.
deficit.description: The yearly gap between government spending and revenue as a share of GDP; negative means a deficit. This is the IMF's general government balance, covering all levels of government, so it differs from the national government deficit the Bureau of the Treasury reports.
deficit.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

current_account.source: World Bank BN.CAB.XOKA.GD.ZS · % of GDP, annual.
current_account.description: The Philippines' overall balance with the rest of the world, trade in goods and services plus net investment income and remittances, as a share of GDP.
current_account.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

fdi.source: World Bank BX.KLT.DINV.WD.GD.ZS · % of GDP, annual.
fdi.description: Money invested into Philippine businesses from abroad each year (foreign direct investment), as a share of GDP.
fdi.dollar: Already expressed as a % of GDP, currency-agnostic. “Dollarise” has no effect on this figure.

fx_usd.source: World Bank series PA.NUS.FCRF · official exchange rate, annual average, shown as US$ per ₱100 (100 ÷ the published PHP per US$).
fx_usd.description: How many US dollars ₱100 buys. A rising number means a stronger peso.
